question: What primary characteristic distinguishes health care waste from ordinary municipal refuse?

options.A: It is generated strictly within surgical and intensive care environments
options.B: It requires immediate chemical stabilization before leaving the bedside
options.C: It is exclusively composed of non-biodegradable plastics and metals
options.D: It contains a high concentration of pathogenic microorganisms and hazardous substances

explanation: Medical waste carries biological agents and toxic materials that pose direct health threats, separating it from standard household garbage. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h1)

question: Why do discarded items like used cotton gauze and blood tubing present significant microbiological dangers?

options.A: They immediately attract vector insects that carry airborne fungal spores
options.B: They release toxic chemical gases upon drying out
options.C: They provide organic moisture and nutrients that support rapid bacterial growth

explanation: Body fluids and organic tissue remnants trapped in porous materials create a fertile breeding ground for infectious agents. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h1)

question: Which color receptacle is universally designated for collecting used hypodermic needles and scalpel blades?
explanation: Sharps require rigid, puncture-proof containers to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries during handling and transport. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h2)

question: What is the primary operational purpose of color-coding waste receptacles in a clinical setting?

options.A: To simplify aesthetic organization within busy hospital wards
options.B: To prevent the dangerous mixing of hazardous materials with general refuse
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing specialized disposal bags
options.D: To comply with international branding standards for pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Color-coding allows immediate visual identification, ensuring that infectious or toxic items do not end up in municipal landfills. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h2)

question: A healthcare worker sustains a puncture injury from a discarded needle left loosely on a medication tray. Which bloodborne pathogens represent the primary transmission risks in this scenario?

options.D: Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV

explanation: Sharps injuries directly inoculate contaminated blood into the vascular system, making bloodborne viral pathogens the chief occupational concern. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common route of pathogen transmission resulting from poorly managed hospital waste?

options.A: Ingestion of contaminated groundwater near open dump sites
options.B: Contact with contaminated items by informal waste pickers
options.C: Direct inhalation of intact viral particles through unbroken skin

explanation: Skin serves as a protective barrier against intact viruses; pathogens typically enter the body through breaks in the skin, mucous membranes, ingestion, or inhalation of aerosols, not directly through healthy skin. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h3)

question: What environmental hazard is created by the open-air burning of medical plastics and PVC packaging?

options.A: Immediate soil alkalization that prevents plant growth
options.B: Depletion of the local groundwater table
options.C: Release of toxic dioxins and furans into the atmosphere

explanation: Low-temperature or open burning of chlorinated plastics creates dangerous chemical pollutants that persist in the environment and harm human health. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h4)

question: Which animal vectors are most commonly attracted to improperly stored organic medical waste in community dumpsites?
explanation: Organic medical waste provides an abundant food source for scavengers and vermin, which then act as vectors spreading disease into nearby communities. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h4)

question: At what capacity should a sharps box or infectious waste bag be securely closed and replaced?

options.A: Whenever an inspector visits the ward
options.B: Only at the end of each calendar week
options.C: When it reaches the three-quarters full mark
options.D: When completely full to maximize storage space

explanation: Stopping at three-quarters capacity prevents overflow, accidental punctures, and spillage during handling and closure. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h5)

question: Why is post-disposal sorting or rummaging through mixed hospital waste strictly prohibited?

options.A: It causes chemical reactions that generate noxious odors
options.B: It drastically increases the incidence of accidental needle-stick injuries and pathogen exposure
options.C: It violates hospital administrative budgeting rules
options.D: It slows down the discharge process for recovering patients

explanation: Attempting to sort mixed waste forces handlers to blindly rifle through dangerous materials, directly exposing them to hidden sharps and infectious matter. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h5)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which an autoclave neutralizes infectious waste?

options.A: High-pressure saturated steam achieving sterilization temperatures
options.B: Chemical oxidation using concentrated chlorine bleach
options.C: Thermal melting via direct open-flame exposure

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to destroy all microbial life on contaminated instruments and medical waste materials. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h6)

question: What purpose does encapsulation serve when managing hazardous medical items like used sharps in resource-constrained facilities?

options.A: It immobilizes and seals waste inside solid blocks of mortar or plastic to prevent access
options.B: It bleaches fabrics to allow safe laundering and reuse
options.C: It converts biohazardous material into organic fertilizer for farming
options.D: It evaporates liquid chemicals into harmless ambient gases

explanation: Encapsulation traps sharps and residues within a solid matrix, preventing scavenging and accidental injuries before final burial. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h6)

question: What is a core clinical responsibility of ward nurses regarding health care waste?

options.C: Purchasing waste receptacles from commercial vendors
options.D: Modeling correct segregation and supervising junior personnel

explanation: Nurses set the standard for safe daily practice on the ward and oversee proper compliance by support staff and students. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h7)

question: A staff nurse notices a junior colleague casually tossing a used syringe into a regular black household waste bin. What is the most appropriate immediate action for the nurse to take?

options.A: Ignore the incident to avoid creating interpersonal tension on the busy ward
options.B: Quietly retrieve the syringe later without mentioning it to anyone
options.C: Report the junior colleague directly to the hospital board for immediate termination
options.D: Correct the action immediately, explaining the biohazard risk and proper bin usage

explanation: Immediate, constructive correction reinforces safety culture and prevents hazardous items from entering municipal waste streams. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h7)
